Data

Database of vertebrate home range sizes. Reference: Tamburello N, Cote IM, Dulvy NK (2015) Energy and the scaling of animal space use. The American Naturalist 186(2):196-211. http://dx.doi.org/10.1086/682070.
Data: http://datadryad.org/resource/doi:10.5061/dryad.q5j65/1

“Homerange” has both numerical and character data, as can be seen in both the str() and glimpse() function. “Homerange” also has several NAs. These two

3. Which animal groups are represented in the data? Make a plot that shows the number in each class.

ggplot(data=homerange,
       mapping=aes(x=class))+
  geom_bar(mapping=aes(fill=class))+
  labs(title="Number of each class")

4. Are there more carnivores or herbivores represented in the data? Make a plot that shows the number in each trophic guild.

ggplot(data=homerange,
       mapping=aes(x=trophic.guild))+
  geom_bar(mapping=aes(fill=trophic.guild))+
  labs(title="# in each trophic guild")

There are more carnivores represented in the data (~340 carnivores vs. ~225 herbivores).

5. Which herbivorous mammals have homeranges greater than 1,000,000 m²? Show only the common name, order, mean homerange size, and mean body mass. Arrange the data in descending order by homerange size and show only the top 10 species.

homerange %>% 
  select(trophic.guild, common.name, order, mean.hra.m2, mean.mass.g) %>% 
  filter(trophic.guild=="herbivore") %>% 
  filter(mean.hra.m2>1000000) %>% 
  slice_min(mean.hra.m2, n=10) %>% 
   arrange(desc(mean.hra.m2))

6. Which two species have the largest and smallest homerange sizes?

homerange %>% 
  select(species, mean.hra.m2) %>% 
  slice_min(mean.hra.m2, n=1)
## # A tibble: 1 × 2
##   species  mean.hra.m2
##   <chr>          <dbl>
## 1 hipoliti        0.03
homerange %>% 
  select(species, mean.hra.m2) %>% 
  slice_max(mean.hra.m2, n=1)
## # A tibble: 1 × 2
##   species  mean.hra.m2

## 1 tarandus  3550830977

7. Which carnivorous mammals have the largest homeranges?

homerange %>% 
  select(species, trophic.guild, mean.hra.m2) %>% 
  filter(trophic.guild=="carnivore") %>% 
  slice_max(mean.hra.m2, n=1)
## # A tibble: 1 × 3
##   species trophic.guild mean.hra.m2
##   <chr>   <chr>               <dbl>
## 1 jubatus carnivore      815060788.

8. Is there a relationship between body mass and homerange size? Make a scatterplot to show this relationship. Be sure to include appropriate labels and a title.

ggplot(data=homerange,
       mapping=aes(x=mean.hra.m2, y=mean.mass.g))+
  geom_point(mapping=aes(color=mean.hra.m2))+
    scale_y_log10()+
    scale_x_log10()+
  geom_smooth(method=lm, se=T)+
  labs(title="body mass (g) vs. homerange size (m^2)")
## `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'

Yes, there is a positive relationship between home range (in meters squared) and body mass (in grams)

9. Use filter to extract the data for only birds and mammals. Then make a plot that compares the homerange sizes of these two groups. Be sure to include appropriate labels and a title.

mammals_and_birds <- filter(homerange, taxon=="mammals" | taxon=="birds")
mammals_and_birds

ggplot(data=mammals_and_birds,
  mapping=aes(x=taxon, y=mean.hra.m2))+
  geom_boxplot(mapping=aes(fill=taxon))+
  scale_y_log10()+
labs(title="homerange size (m^2) of mammals vs. birds")

10. Do one additional exploratory analysis of your choice. Before writing the code, write the question you are trying to answer. The question should be biologically meaningful and appropriate for the data. It must include at least one filter(), select(), and arrange().

Which mammals have a homerange smaller than or equal to 30,000 m^2? Find the top 20 in ascending order and include common name, locomotion, homerange, and mass.

homerange %>% 
  select(trophic.guild, taxon, common.name, locomotion, mean.hra.m2, mean.mass.g) %>% 
  filter(taxon=="mammals") %>% 
  filter(trophic.guild=="carnivore") %>% 
  filter(mean.hra.m2<=30000) %>% 
  slice_min(mean.hra.m2, n=20) %>% 
   arrange(mean.hra.m2)
